item.title: On blow-up dynamics for the nonlinear wave equation and the harmonic map heat flow
item.description:
arXiv:2611.06959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This Ph.D. thesis concerns the blow-up analysis, and more precisely, the asymptotic decomposition into profiles of solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations. In Chapter 1, we present a unifying framework for finding profile decompositions in Hilbert spaces using the notion of dislocation spaces. The next chapters are then devoted to my publications. In the second chapter, we construct solutions to the focusing, energy-critical, nonlinear wave equation in dimension 4 and 5, exhibiting finite-time Type II blow-up precisely at the origin with a single profile and a prescribed polynomial blow-up rate of order $-1-
u$, where $
u > 1$ in 4D and $
u > 3$ in 5D. The major difference between dimension 4 and 5 consists in the renormalization procedure. In 4D, we essentially follow the Krieger-Schlag-Tataru scheme developed for the 3-dimensional equation, where the polynomial structure of the nonlinearity permits the use of simple algebraic manipulations to control error terms. By contrast, the 5D case requires a modified setup due to the lower regularity of the nonlinearity, which complicates the treatment of nonlinear error terms. In Chapter 3, we provide a modern presentation of classical Lp and Schauder estimates for parabolic equations. Then, in Chapter 4, we consider finite-time and $k$-equivariant solutions to the harmonic map heat flow from a disk to a sphere. Under general time-dependent, $k$-equivariant and smooth boundary data, we prove that the profile decomposition at the singular time contains only one bubble. The method relies on the maximum and comparison principle. We also prove a global existence criterion and exhibit solutions blowing up in infinite time for any degree of equivariance. Finally, the appendix presents the profile decomposition for the harmonic map heat flow proved by Struwe and Qing using energy arguments and the Palais-Smale condition.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Samuelian

item.title: Regularity Theory for the Equation $\det(D^2u) = f(u)$ in Two Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.06978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the interior regularity of convex solutions to $$\det D^2u = f(u)$$ in planar domains, with no regularity or monotonicity assumptions on $f$. In particular, when $f$ is bounded between positive constants, we show that $u$ is locally $C^{1,\,1}$, and that its level sets near a critical point are asymptotically ellipses. Our analysis relies on a new monotone quantity for a second-order flow satisfied by the support functions of the level sets of $u$. As a byproduct of our methods, we obtain Liouville theorems that generalize a classical result of J\"{o}rgens, and include a complete classification of global solutions in 2D to an obstacle problem studied by Jin-Tu-Xiong. As another application, we obtain regularity and rigidity results for rotating-wave solutions of the semigeostrophic equations from meteorology.
item.dc:creator: Connor Mooney, Aranya Sen

item.title: An Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom law for a kinematic model of turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2611.07076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom-type law for passive scalars advected by a family of random $C^\alpha$ velocity field proposed in \cite{JDEMS} as a kinematic model of turbulent fluids. Up to a technical assumption on one parameter, the expectation of the squared $L^2_t H^\gamma_x$ norm of solutions to the passive scalar equation is bounded by the squared $L^2$ norm of the deterministic initial datum, uniformly in the viscosity, whenever $\alpha + 2\gamma < 1$. The proof is based on a new insight in the theory developed by \cite{FM} to prove Richardson's dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the same model.
item.dc:creator: Camillo De Lellis

item.title: Fundamental solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian in cone-like domains, with applications to Liouville-type theorems and global H\"older regularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.07157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $ C_\omega$ be the cone generated by a proper $C^2$ domain $\omega\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$. We study positive homogeneous solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation in $C_\omega$ with zero exterior values. For $p\ne2$, the operator is nonlinear and not uniformly elliptic. For every $p>1$, we identify two extremal homogeneities $\beta^+>0>\beta^-$, prove that every fundamental solution, if one exists, has one of these exponents, and construct homogeneous eigenfunctions whose eigenvalues have signs determined by the position of the homogeneity relative to $\beta^\pm$. As an application, we obtain the Lane-Emden threshold $q^*=p-1+sp/\beta^+$ for every $p>1$: nontrivial nonnegative supersolutions of $(-\Delta_p)^s u\ge u^q$ in $C_\omega$ do not exist for $0<q<q^*$, whereas homogeneous supersolutions exist for $q>q^*$. We also establish Hopf-type lower bounds at conical boundary points with the optimal exponent. When $p-1>sp$ , we construct both fundamental solutions, one singular at the vertex and the other vanishing there. For $p=2$, these solutions are known; our method recovers them for every $s\in(0,1)$. The homogeneous eigenfunctions also serve as barriers, yielding boundary decay and global H\"older regularity for $(-\Delta_p)^s u=f$ in bounded Lipschitz domains, with zero exterior values and $f$ continuous up to the boundary. The admissible H\"older exponents are determined by the exterior cones. All results hold for every $N\ge2$; in particular, $N>sp$ is not needed.
item.dc:creator: Reshmi Biswas, Alexander Quaas

item.title: Orbital stability and instability of standing waves for an inhomogeneous logarithmic Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.07167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the inhomogeneous logarithmic Schr\"odinger equation \[ i\partial_tu+\Delta u+|x|^{-1}u\log|u|^2=0, \qquad (t,x)\in\R\times\R^N,\quad N\ge2. \] For every initial datum in $H^1(\R^N)$, we establish global existence of weak solutions. We also construct explicit positive stationary solutions and solve the associated Nehari minimization problem. For $\omega\ge0$, the minimizer is unique up to {a constant} phase and is given by \[ e^{\frac{N-1}{2}(1+\sqrt{1+\omega})} e^{-(1+\sqrt{1+\omega})|x|}, \] whereas for $\omega<0$ the infimum is zero and is not attained. Finally, we prove that the standing waves associated with these profiles are orbitally stable for $\omega>0$ by a variational argument, and orbitally unstable for $-1<\omega<-1+(N-1)^{-2}$ by combining spectral analysis, localized energy and mass estimates, and phase modulation.
item.dc:creator: Alex H. Ardila

item.title: Energy methods and optimal decay for time-fractional equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.07185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study energy methods for the time-fractional equation $\partial_t^\alpha(u-u_0)-(a(t,x)u_x)_x+(F(t,x,u))_x=Q(t,x,u)$ on the real line, where $0<\alpha<1$, the coefficient $a$ is measurable and bounded from above and from below by positive constants, $\sigma\partial_xF\ge0$, $\sigma Q\le0$, and the data are in $L^1\cap L^\infty$. Using Yosida approximations of the kernel, an iteration on the $L^{2^m}$ norms gives the parabolic decay $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le C\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-\alpha/2}$. In $L^2$ it gives the rate $t^{-\alpha/4}$, which, already for the linear equation, improves the rate $t^{-\alpha/5}$ obtained before by the classical energy method. For the convection--diffusion equation $\partial_t^\alpha(u-u_0)-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, the parabolic rate is optimal for $q\ge2$, and for $1<q<2$ the convection improves it. An $L^1$ time-regularity estimate of B\'enilan--Crandall type gives the pointwise flux bound $|u|^{q-1}u-u_x=O(\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-\alpha})$. This bound takes the place of the Ole\u{\i}nik estimate and yields the optimal rate $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim t^{-\alpha/q}$ for $1<q<2$. For nonnegative data, matching lower bounds hold for the $L^p$ norms.
item.dc:creator: Liviu I. Ignat

item.title: Multiplicity and least energy sign-changing normalized solutions for a Kirchhoff equation on bounded domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.07199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study sign-changing normalized solutions of the Kirchhoff problem \[ \begin{cases} -\left(a+b\displaystyle\int_\Omega|\nabla u|^2\,dx\right)\Delta u =|u|^{p-2}u+\mu u &\text{in }\Omega,\\ u=0 &\text{on }\partial\Omega, \end{cases} \] subject to the constraint \[ \int_\Omega |u|^2\,dx=c, \] where $a,b>0$, $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N$ is a smooth bounded connected domain, $1\le N\le3$, $c>0$ is prescribed, and $\mu\in\mathbb R$ is a Lagrange multiplier. We assume $2<p<\infty$ for $N=1,2$ and $2<p\le6$ for $N=3$. For every integer $k\ge1$, we obtain at least $k$ distinct pairs of sign-changing normalized solutions for sufficiently small $c>0$. We determine the small mass asymptotics of their energies, Lagrange multipliers, and rescaled profiles in terms of the distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues and their eigenspaces. When $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$, we obtain infinitely many such pairs for every prescribed mass $c>0$, with energies tending to $+\infty$. At $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$, this conclusion holds for every sufficiently small fixed mass. We also establish the existence of a least energy sign-changing normalized solution on general bounded domains for every prescribed mass when $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$. For sufficiently small mass, such a solution exists on general bounded domains when $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$ and on star-shaped domains when $p>2+\frac{8}{N}$. For any family of such least energy solutions, the rescaled profiles approach the $L^2$-unit sphere of the second Dirichlet eigenspace in $H_0^1(\Omega)$ as $c\to0^+$. The finite multiplicity and least energy results include the Sobolev critical case $N=3$, $p=6$. The proofs combine a localized symmetric minimax construction, energy comparisons with one-signed critical points, and compactness arguments that preserve the sign-changing property.
item.dc:creator: Qun Wang, Xiaojun Chang

item.title: Non-migration for planar elastic flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.07242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a closed planar curve evolving by the free or the length-preserving elastic flow. We prove that the scale-invariant bound $L\int k^2\,ds\le 4\pi^2+8/3$ at the initial time prevents the entire curve from crossing any line between two times. For the free flow, the proof combines a monotonicity estimate for the normalized bending energy with a barrier that compares centroid motion to an expanding energy radius. For the length-preserving flow, a quantitative gradient estimate controls the total centroid displacement.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Novaga

item.title: Well-posedness and large deviations for 3D primitive equations with jumps
item.description: arXiv:2611.07274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the global pathwise well-posedness and a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for the three-dimensional viscous primitive equations driven by multiplicative L\'evy noise represented by a compensated Poisson random measure. Under local Lipschitz and moment growth assumptions on the noise coefficient, we construct local martingale solutions and obtain a unique maximal pathwise solution with c\`adl\`ag trajectories in the $H^1$ energy space. Additional sixth-moment growth in $H^1$ and $L^6$ growth bounds on the baroclinic component of the noise yield global pathwise well-posedness. The proof combines the jump It\^o formula with baroclinic and anisotropic energy estimates to rule out finite-time blow-up. Under further exponential integrability and structural assumptions on the noise coefficient, we establish a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle in a strong path topology by the weak convergence approach.
item.dc:creator: Zhuoyang Shen, Xinhua Li, Chunyou Sun

item.title: Boltzmann equations with dilatation and shear: global well-posedness and stability
item.description: arXiv:2611.07340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study global well-posedness and stability for Boltzmann equations with linear velocity deformation, allowing for arbitrarily large deformation strength. For diagonal dilatation with $-2<\gamma\leq0$ and cylindrical dilatation with $-3/2<\gamma\leq0$, with or without shear, we construct global homogeneous solutions for small data and prove their stability under small spatially inhomogeneous perturbations. In scaled variables, the perturbations remain uniformly controlled in deformation-adapted spaces and decay in mixed spatial--velocity norms, algebraically in the diagonal regime and exponentially in the cylindrical regime. For homogeneous simple shear with $-2\leq\gamma\leq0$, we prove global existence and uniqueness for nonnegative data with finite mass and Fisher information, without smallness or a finite-energy assumption. These solutions conserve mass and propagate additional Sobolev regularity. For spatially inhomogeneous simple shear with $-2<\gamma\leq0$, we establish global well-posedness for small data. The analysis combines commuting vector fields, dispersive and bilinear collision estimates, and integrability of the rescaled collision coefficients. For homogeneous shear, a positivity-preserving splitting transfers Fisher-information control to rough data, while a Lorentz-space estimate includes the endpoint $\gamma=-2$ in the global continuation argument.
item.dc:creator: Shuangqian Liu, Haoran Peng, Jiatong Zou

item.title: Finite-Support Approximation in Variable-Coefficient Sobolev Spaces on Nonhomogeneous Flow-Measure Trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.07350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T$ be a nonhomogeneous rooted tree equipped with a positive flow measure $m$. For $1<p<\infty$, consider the variable-coefficient Sobolev space on the nonhomogeneous flow-measure tree~$T$ \[ W_a^{1,p}(T,m) = \left\{ f\in L^p(T,m): \sum_{x\ne \rho}a(x)m(x)\lvert f(x)-f(\pi(x))\rvert^p<\infty \right\}, \] where $a$ is a positive variable coefficient, $\rho$ denotes the root and $\pi(x)$ denotes the parent of $x$. Using an averaging method over descendant levels, we prove the density of finitely supported functions in $W_a^{1,p}(T,m)$ for coefficients satisfying a weighted moment condition. As an application, the relationship between solutions on finite domains and global solutions is clarified for $p=2$.
item.dc:creator: Zeyu Cheng, Yichun Zhao, Jiang Zhou

item.title: Infinitely many nonradial positive solutions for two-coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations in $\bbr^N$ without symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.07359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the following two-coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations: \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} &-\Delta u+P(x)u=\mu u^3+\beta uv^2,\quad\text{in }\R^N,\\ &-\Delta v+Q(x)v=\nu v^3+\beta u^2v,\quad\text{in }\R^N,\\ &u,\,v\in H^1(\R^N) \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $N=2,3$, $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are potentials, $\mu$ and $\nu$ are positive coefficients and $\beta\in\R\setminus\{0\}$ is the coupling parameter. By developing the intermediate reduction arguments in [del Pino-Wei-Yao, Calc. Var., 2015], we prove the existence of infinitely many nonradial positive solutions to the above system under suitable regularity and decay conditions on $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$, {\bf but without any symmetry assumptions on them}. The scalar version of our result also gives {\bf a positive answer} to the first part of [Question~3, del Pino-Wei-Yao, Calc. Var., 2015] and our method might be helpful in studying other problems.
item.dc:creator: Rui He, Xiangqing Liu, Qingfang Wang, Yuanze Wu

item.title: Preservation and Loss of Log-Concavity in the Repulsive Vlasov--Poisson System
item.description: arXiv:2611.07380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pr\'ekopa's theorem shows that, for jointly log-concave initial data, free transport preserves the log-concavity of spatial densities. This paper asks whether this property persists in the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system. In dimensions two and higher, we construct smooth, strongly log-concave initial distributions whose spatial densities lose log-concavity at arbitrarily small positive times. For one-dimensional cold-ion data, we prove that the spatial density remains log-concave for all time.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoxiao Sun, Zhaopeng Wang

item.title: Asymptotic behavior of an integral equation of Landau-Lifschitz type
item.description: arXiv:2611.07391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study an integral equation of Landau-Lifschitz-type involving the Riesz potential $$ u(x)=\ell+C_*\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\frac{u(y)(|\nabla u(y)|^{2}+|u_k(y)|^2)-u_k(y)e_k}{|x-y|^{n-\alpha}}dy, $$ where $\ell \in \mathbb{R}^k$ is a constant vector, $C_* \neq 0$ is a constant, $u\colon\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{S}^{k-1}:=\{u=(u_1,u_2,\cdots,u_k) \in {{\mathbb{R}}^{k}};|u|=1\}$, $k \geq 1$, $n \geq 2$, and $0<\alpha<n$. We provide a decay rate at which $|u_k|$ converges to zero under some mild conditions. This argument still works for the Ginzburg-Landau-type integral equation.
item.dc:creator: Tiantian Zhou

item.title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
item.description: arXiv:2611.07395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a computational framework that combines machine-learning-based discovery with rigorous computer-assisted numerical certification and formal verification for strongly nonlinear partial differential equations. We demonstrate the approach for periodic gravity-capillary traveling water waves. Physics-informed neural networks are used as a search mechanism, with the wave profile, wave speed and, in continuation experiments, surface tension learned directly from the governing equations without training data. Through a staged training and refinement procedure, the neural networks achieve near-machine-precision residuals of the governing equations, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. A single formulation recovers high-amplitude Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples. Continuation from a high-amplitude Wilton ripple in surface tension reveals new high-amplitude candidate solutions. We freeze one candidate as an explicit finite representation and rigorously certify a uniform bound on its governing-equation residual using interval arithmetic, accounting for floating-point roundoff, Fourier truncation, aliasing and grid-to-continuum errors. This independently validates the neural-network accuracy. We formalize the certification argument in Lean, which machine-checks the deductions from certified numerical bounds to the residual theorem. Both the interval certification and formalization were developed with substantial assistance from a large language model, while the validity of the result remains independent of the language model: the numerical bounds are rigorously enclosed by interval arithmetic and the subsequent mathematical deductions are checked by the Lean kernel. Together, these steps provide a pipeline from neural discovery to rigorous numerical certification and machine-checked verification with auditable mathematical guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Michal Shavit, Yongji Wang, Tristan Buckmaster

item.title: The interface scattering law for run-and-tumble kinetic models
item.description: arXiv:2611.07409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For microorganisms with run-and-tumble motility, kinetic models provide a well-established description of transport in smoothly varying environments. Sharp signal changes, however, can induce asymmetric interface responses. A motivating example is the response to dark-light boundaries: cells moving into the light largely maintain their direction, whereas those entering the dark are effectively scattered back. Through an interface-layer analysis of pathway-based kinetic equations, we formally derive effective interface conditions for the limiting run-and-tumble model. These velocity-nonlocal conditions capture non-adiabatic scattering near signal discontinuities, linking intracellular sensory dynamics to transport across sharp environmental boundaries. For a two-velocity model, they reduce to an explicit transmission matrix. We assess the interface law numerically using biologically motivated parameters for E. coli chemotaxis.
item.dc:creator: Shicong Lei, Jiangyan Liang, Weiran Sun, Min Tang

item.title: Finiteness of singularities for higher-weight axially symmetric minimizers of the relaxed Dirichlet energy
item.description: arXiv:2611.07414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k\ge2$ be an integer. We prove that every minimizer of the Bethuel--Brezis--Coron relaxed Dirichlet energy in the signed meridional $k$-axial class, with continuous $H^1$ degree-zero data on the boundary of a ball, is smooth outside a finite subset of the symmetry axis. This extends the weight-one finiteness theorem of Hardt--Lin--Poon and resolves the finite-singularity question posed by Martinazzi--Rivi\`ere as Open Problem~A, in the fixed-boundary Bethuel--Brezis--Coron setting with continuous degree-zero data. The interior argument uses a distributional graph-boundary identity, height-preserving half-turn replacements, and exact square completions retaining the current cost. Cap-valued crosscuts and a finite incidence count exclude singular accumulation at the boundary poles.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyuan Dai, Huaijie Wang, Wei Wang

item.title: Dispersive estimates for Dirac equations in Aharonov-Bohm magnetic fields: massive case
item.description: arXiv:2611.07445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dispersive properties of the massive Dirac equation perturbed by an Aharonov-Bohm magnetic field, proving in particular dispersive and Strichartz estimates for the associated flow. This paper is the natural continuation of our previous work in the massless case [3], and the overall structure of the analysis remains similar. The presence of a nonzero mass term, however, breaks the scaling invariance of the equation and introduces new difficulties at several stages of the argument. In particular, the appearance of the spectral thresholds +m and -m leads to a genuinely different low energy regime, which requires a separate analysis of the singular angular component.
item.dc:creator: Federico Cacciafesta, Piero D'Ancona, Zhiqing Yin, Junyong Zhang

item.title: H^{s,p} estimates for weak solutions of fractional nonlocal equations in divergence form
item.description: arXiv:2611.07606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes interior $H^{s,p}$ regularity for weak solutions to fractional nonlocal equations in divergence form with general kernels. Under the $(\delta, R)$-vanishing condition on the coefficients, we prove that for $p>2$, if the source term $f\in L^p_{loc}$, then the solution $u\in H^{s,p}_{loc}$. In contrast to Byun and Kim \cite{BK2025}, our result holds in the borderline case for $f$ without requiring differentiability assumptions. Our approach simplifies previous methods by using the stability properties of the fractional gradient to derive the good-inequality directly, thereby avoiding reliance on maximal functions. The proof integrates Vitali's covering lemma, Hardy-Littlewood maximal theory, self-improving estimates, and compactness arguments. This work extends classical $W^{1,p}$ regularity to fractional nonlocal settings under minimal kernel assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Zhenjie Li, Lihe Wang, Chunqin Zhou

item.title: Sharp singular Moser-Trudinger inequalities and n-Laplacian equations with degenerate potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.07628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n\geq2$, $0<\beta<n$, and let $V$ be a continuous nonnegative potential on $\R^n$ with a positive lower bound outside a ball. Under the constraint $\int_{\R^n}(|\nabla u|^n+V|u|^n)\dd\leq1$, we prove the singular Moser--Trudinger inequality with sharp coefficient $(1-\beta/n)\alpha_n$, where $\alpha_n=n|\mathbb S^{n-1}|^{1/(n-1)}$. The subcritical supremum is attained for every such potential. If $V$ is radial and $r^\beta V(r)$ is nondecreasing, the critical supremum is also attained. This includes potentials that vanish on a ball and decrease to a positive limit at infinity. Under the same radial hypothesis, a bound for the tangential gradient shows that every extremal is radial and that the tangential gradients of maximizing sequences converge to zero in $L^n$, including at the critical coefficient. For the singular $n$-Laplacian equation with critical exponential growth, we obtain an explicit sufficient level for Palais--Smale compactness. Under the Ambrosetti--Rabinowitz condition and a smallness assumption at zero, this gives a nonzero nonnegative mountain-pass solution for all sufficiently large coupling parameters.
item.dc:creator: Hao Hu, Yanjun Liu, Huabo Zhang

item.title: Classification and asymptotics for the boundary Yamabe equation with an isolated singularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.07636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify positive singular solutions of the boundary Yamabe equation on the punctured half-space in every dimension $n\ge3$. Previous symmetry results reduce this problem to a nonlinear PDE in two variables, for which classical phase-plane methods are unavailable. We develop a Hamiltonian method that combines local bifurcation with compactness to prove that every nonstationary cylindrical profile of a singular solution is periodic and uniquely determined, up to translation, by its Hamiltonian energy. At each stationary or periodic profile, the space of solutions of the linearized equation is two-dimensional. Finally, every positive solution in a half-ball with a nonremovable isolated boundary singularity is asymptotic to a unique global singular solution, with an algebraically decaying relative error.
item.dc:creator: Tianling Jin, Yuxuan Liao, Jingang Xiong

item.title: Determination of the Lam\'e parameters and density at a fixed frequency
item.description: arXiv:2611.07642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish global uniqueness for the inverse boundary value problem of three-dimensional time-harmonic isotropic elasticity with smooth real Lam\'e parameters satisfying strong convexity and a smooth positive mass density. At a fixed known nonzero frequency for which the corresponding Dirichlet problems are uniquely solvable, the full displacement-to-traction map uniquely determines all three coefficients. The proof first recovers the full boundary Taylor expansions of $\lambda$, $\mu$, and $\rho$, and derives an exact Green--Betti identity for a four-component reduction, with the terms involving $W=\omega^2\rho$ and $\nabla W$ retained. Three independent physical polarizations of the rank-three characteristic quotient yield a complete $3\times3$ matrix of polynomial moment identities. A Cauchy transform construction produces an exact relative transport matrix $H$, normalized to $I_3$ in a common exterior region. Its invertibility follows from the determinant identity $\det H=\sqrt{\mu_2/\mu_1}>0$. Holomorphic dependence on the projective null direction, established by differentiating the transport equation at a fixed physical point, leads to a finite-type rigidity system that determines the Lam\'e parameters. Finally, products of physical elastic solutions and Fourier uniqueness recover the mass density.
item.dc:creator: Huaian Diao, Yang Dong, Umidjon Durdiev, Weisheng Zhou

item.title: Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the random velocity model with controlled sweeping
item.description: arXiv:2611.07694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The present paper establishes the Richardson dispersion law, predicting the particle separation with time according to $\E R_t^2 \sim t^3$, as well as anomalous dissipation for the associated tracer, for a random H\"older continuous velocity vectorfield with controlled sweeping.
item.dc:creator: Charles Fefferman, Svitlana Mayboroda

item.title: Critical Curve for Three-Dimensional Radial Wave Systems with Distinct Speeds
item.description: arXiv:2611.07710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study radially symmetric solutions to the three-dimensional semilinear wave system with distinct propagation speeds \[ u_{tt}-c_1^2\Delta u=|v_t|^p\ , \ v_{tt}-c_2^2\Delta v=|u_t|^q\ , \ c_1, c_2>0\ , c_1\neq c_2\ . \] For \(1<p,q<2\), we prove that \[ \Gamma(p,q) = 2+\max\left\{\frac1p,\frac1q\right\}-pq=0 \] is the exact critical curve separating small-data global existence from finite-time blow-up. More precisely, sufficiently small, compactly supported radial initial data give rise to global solutions when $\Gamma(p,q)<0$. On the other hand, for a class of initial data, the corresponding solutions blow up in finite time, with an upper bound for the lifespan, when $\Gamma(p,q)\geq 0$.
item.dc:creator: Wei Dai, Mengyun Liu, Chengbo Wang

item.title: Global existence of solutions to the 2D compressible nematic liquid crystal flows with large initial data and vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2611.07725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For periodic initial data that allow vacuum, we establish the global-in-time existence of solutions to the 2D compressible nematic liquid crystal flows, under the condition that the bulk viscosity coefficient is sufficiently large and a geometric angular constraint is imposed on the initial direction field. Our results remain valid for arbitrarily large initial energy. Furthermore, under appropriate additional assumptions imposed on the pressure, we also establish the uniqueness of the constructed solutions.
item.dc:creator: Qiao Liu, Qingkui Ma, Fuyi Xu

item.title: Global well-posedness for the energy-critical focusing NLS on $\mathbb T^3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.07740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove global well-posedness for the focusing quintic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the standard three-dimensional torus for initial data below the mass-corrected energy and Sobolev-norm thresholds determined by the Euclidean ground state. This gives a subthreshold focusing counterpart to the defocusing theorem of Ionescu and Pausader. The proof combines the periodic profile analysis with the recent nonradial Euclidean scattering theorem of Su and Zhao. The mass correction yields an invariant region and a nonnegative energy decomposition, placing every Euclidean profile below both ground-state thresholds. Uniform bounds on finite intervals follow from a contradiction argument on shrinking time intervals.
item.dc:creator: Meng Chen, Han Wang

item.title: Second-order geometric consistency of nonlinear FE-HMM on surfaces via corrector non-degeneracy
item.description: arXiv:2611.07761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the geometric variational crime of nonlinear finite element heterogeneous multiscale methods (FE--HMM) for $p$-growth monotone laws on curved surfaces, $p\ge2$. The practical method projects discrete gradients onto the exact tangent planes; we compare it with the exactly lifted method on the same discrete space. Without further hypotheses, the difference is $O(h_g^{p/(p-1)})$ in the metric induced by the cell correctors. The optimal order $O(h_g^2)$ holds with a constant given by a weighted negative moment of the corrected gradients, evaluated along the practical solution only; no bounds on discrete gradients in $L^\infty$ are used. The negative moment is a sufficient condition for the lower shifted $p$-structure of the discrete homogenized flux, which for $p>2$ is not available in general. For the model law and a fixed cell mesh, its uniform boundedness is equivalent to a finite-dimensional directional criterion on degenerate correctors, and for laminates it holds with an explicit bound, uniform in the cell mesh. With macro--micro quasi-optimality and an estimate for coefficient sampling, the reconstructed microscopic field converges as $O(h+H^{\min{s,1}}+h_g^2)$, where $H^s$ is the cell approximation rate. Experiments on a torus with an exact closest-point lift and a transported anisotropic $p=4$ material show second-order geometric convergence up to $98,304$ macroscopic quadrature points, each with a fully solved nonlinear cell problem, with bounded a posteriori constants for both load treatments.
item.dc:creator: Marcial Nguemfouo

item.title: Instability of Self-Similar Implosions for the Compressible Euler Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.07762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that all known regular self-similar implosion solutions of the isentropic compressible Euler equations are unstable to shock formation. The perturbations can be chosen to be small in a class determined by the regularity threshold of the background. The proof relies on an amplification mechanism which occurs along the surface of the backward sonic cone from the implosion point. Motivated by our main results, we formulate an implosion censorship conjecture for the compressible Euler equations, stating that classical implosions are unstable to shock formation.
item.dc:creator: Serban Cicortas, Igor Rodnianski, Ely Sandine

item.title: Singular viscosity-exponent limit for one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations with far field vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2611.07790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the limit $\delta\to1^+$ for the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations with viscosity $\mu(\rho)=\rho^\delta$ and far field vacuum. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result on the viscosity-exponent limit $\delta\to1^+$ for strong solutions with far field vacuum. With far field vacuum, the diffusion coefficient $\rho^{\delta-1}$ does not converge uniformly to $1$ on $\mathbb R$ as $\delta\to1^+$. The main difficulty is to obtain uniform estimates for this limit. By introducing some new weighted density variables, we establish local well-posedness and uniform estimates without requiring $\rho_0^{(\delta-1)/2}\in L^2(\mathbb R)$. We prove strong convergence to the known global $\delta=1$ solution obtained in \cite{WenZhangDCDS2025} on a local time interval independent of $\delta$. With one additional order of regularity of the initial data and the limit solution, the convergence holds on every fixed finite time interval, and the maximal life-spans of the $\delta>1$ solutions tend to $+\infty$ as $\delta\to1^+$.
item.dc:creator: Xingyang Zhang

item.title: A Lagrangian Approach to Uniqueness for Active Scalars in Generalized Mean Oscillation Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.07834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified Lagrangian framework for the uniqueness of weak solutions to a broad class of two-dimensional inviscid active scalar equations in generalized mean oscillation spaces. Under common structural assumptions on the Biot--Savart kernels, we identify mean oscillation spaces that ensure an Osgood condition for the velocity, and establish uniqueness in these classes. For the two-dimensional Euler equations, we establish uniqueness for vorticities whose mean oscillation grows mildly at small scales, extending beyond $\mathrm{BMO}$. For the surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) and incompressible porous media (IPM) equations, we obtain uniqueness in spaces logarithmically rougher than $C^{0,1}$. We also obtain what are (to our knowledge) the strongest known uniqueness results for the $\alpha$-SQG equation, $0<\alpha<1$, in spaces logarithmically rougher than critical H\"older spaces $C^\alpha$. The framework also applies to various logarithmically perturbed models, yielding uniqueness in the corresponding sharp regularity classes. The proof combines a sharp regularity estimate for the velocity with a stability estimate for integral operators under measure-preserving rearrangements. This provides a single uniqueness argument for the entire family under common structural assumptions on the kernels.
item.dc:creator: Hyunjin In, Dong-ha Kim, Junha Kim, Seungjae Lee

item.title: Quantifying and minimizing collision intensity in stationary crowd flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.07837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a continuum model to quantify kinematic collision risk in stationary crowd flow. From the density-weighted inward relative flux, we derive a collision functional based on the symmetric velocity gradient. For incompressible flows with constant density, this functional is convex and positively homogeneous of degree one in a combination of second derivatives of the stream function. We minimize it subject to prescribed boundary flux. On bounded simply connected domains with Lipschitz boundary, under a finite-energy lifting assumption, we prove existence of minimizers in a relaxed class that allows this derivative combination to be a vector-valued Radon measure. We show that disks are the only domains with a nontrivial zero-trace kernel, corresponding to rigid rotation about the center. Using the compact embedding for functions of bounded deformation, we prove that relaxed energy sublevels are compact without normalization on every other admissible domain, and after removing one rotational component on disks. We identify the relaxed functional with the strong $W^{1,1}$ lower semicontinuous envelope of the functional on the prescribed-trace class with integrable controlled derivatives. Then, we derive optimality conditions via convex duality. We construct explicit radial flows on annular sectors and prove that they minimize the energy over the full admissible classes, including nonradial competitors. On the square, distinct minimizers with the same prescribed boundary flux have different local collision intensities. The square--disk comparison shows that the saddle flow loses optimality when the domain changes, even after normalization.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Ashrafyan, Diogo A. Gomes

item.title: Liouville systems I: Blow-up analysis and orthogonal decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.07857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study blow-up solutions of generalized Liouville systems on a closed surface at and near critical parameter hypersurfaces. Under a Morse assumption on the reduced functional, we establish the following results. First, we introduce amplitude variables in the approximate manifold and prove that every sequence of blow-up solutions at a fixed critical parameter, or along an admissible sequence from the lower side, admits a unique minimizing decomposition up to permutation. The remainder converges to zero and is orthogonal to the center, scale, and amplitude directions. The concentration scales are comparable, the limiting configuration satisfies the scale balance conditions, and the amplitudes vanish after multiplication by the logarithmic scale. Second, we determine the leading parameter defect in both critical decay regimes and prove that, along each fixed admissible path, all sufficiently large solutions lie in finitely many disjoint bubbling neighborhoods. Finally, assuming the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical configuration, the solution set at the fixed critical parameter is compact. These results provide the analytic foundation for studying the resonant degree via critical points at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Mohameden Ahmedou, Zhengni Hu, Jonas Fey, Lei Zhang

item.title: Global Solvability in Critical Sobolev Spaces for divergence-type equations associated with elliptic systems of vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.07904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present global solvability results, in critical Sobolev spaces, for divergence-type equations associated with elliptic systems of vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Bousquet, Laurent Moonens, Tiago Picon, Emmanuel Russ

item.title: Log-concavity and level set curvature estimates for the first Dirichlet eigenfunction in hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2611.07907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the first Dirichlet eigenfunction on bounded, smooth and strictly horo-convex domains in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We prove its strict $\log$-concavity in arbitrary dimension and establish the Gauss curvature bound $K>1$ for its level sets. In dimensions two and three, we further obtain quantitative lower bounds for $K$ in terms of the minimum Gauss curvature of the boundary. In higher dimensions, the product of the two smallest principal curvatures of each level hypersurface exceeds one. Furthermore, we extend the strict $\log$-concavity result to bounded smooth horo-convex domains. Our approach combines maximum or minimum principles for suitable auxiliary functions, boundary convexity estimates and a domain deformation argument.
item.dc:creator: Wei Zhang, Qi Zhou

item.title: Multiplicity via symmetry for the Minkowski mean curvature equation: Dirichlet and Neumann problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.07963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Minkowski mean curvature equation $$ -\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =\lambda u+\mu h(x,u) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \quad \mathcal B u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial \Omega, $$ where $\mathcal B \in \{ \mathcal D, \mathcal N \}$ is a Dirichlet or Neumann boundary condition and $\Omega$ is a smooth bounded domain, required to be convex in the Neumann case. Moreover, $\lambda, \mu \geq0$ are parameters, and $h(x,u)$ is odd with respect to $u$ and positive for $u > 0$. Using minmax methods in nonsmooth critical point theory, we prove that $\lambda>\lambda^\mathcal B_k$ yields at least $k$ pairs of nontrivial solutions with negative energy for every $\mu\geq0$, where $\lambda_k^\mathcal B$ are the corresponding Laplacian eigenvalues, indexed by $\lambda^\mathcal B_0=0$. Moreover, if $H(x,u):=\int_0^u h(x,t)\,dt=o(u^2)$ as $u\to0$, we prove that for $\lambda\in[\lambda^\mathcal B_k,\lambda^\mathcal B_{k+1})$ and every $j\geq\max\{1,k\}$, sufficiently large $\mu$ yields at least $2j-k$ distinct pairs of solutions: $j$ with negative energy and $j-k$ with positive energy.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Boscaggin, Ricardo Ziegele

item.title: Hypocoercivity for a thermostatted Boltzmann equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.07999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Boltzmann equation for a gas on the three-dimensional torus. Its particles collide with one another and with a thermal reservoir whose temperature varies in space. The reservoir heats the gas in some regions and cools it in others, driving a nonequilibrium energy current. For the isotropic cutoff kernel, with Maxwell molecules or hard potentials, we prove global well-posedness and exponential convergence to the same stationary state for initial data with a common Gaussian upper bound and Gaussian moment bound. These bounds determine how weak self collisions must be relative to bath collisions. The estimates are uniform over bath profiles between fixed positive temperature bounds. For any nonconstant reservoir profile on the three-dimensional torus, this stationary state cannot be a local Maxwellian. When particles collide only with the bath, relative entropy to the stationary state cannot increase. Once self collisions are added, arbitrarily small perturbations can initially increase it, even though they later return exponentially.
item.dc:creator: Josephine Evans, Alexander Pilakoutas

item.title: The Short Pulse equation on the half lines: a Riemann--Hilbert approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.08105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we analyze the initial boundary value (IBV) problems for the Short Pulse (SP) equation $u_{xt}=u+\frac{1}{6}(u^3)_{xx}$ (classical solutions) on the half-lines $x\ge 0$ and $x\le 0$ under the condition of sufficient decay as $x\to +\infty$ or as $x\to -\infty$. Using the Riemann--Hilbert (RH) problem approach, we show that these two IBV problems differ substantially regarding the boundary values required for problems to be well-posed. Namely, the solution of the ``right problem'' ($x\ge 0$) is uniquely determined by the initial data $u(x,0)$, $x\ge 0$ alone, whereas for the ``left problem'' ($x\le 0$), two boundary functions $u(0,t)$ and $u_x(0,t)$ have to be prescribed, together with the initial data, for a well-posed problem.
item.dc:creator: Iryna Karpenko, Dmitry Shepelsky

item.title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy for a critical Choquard equation with Hardy potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.08146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the critical Choquard equation \[ -\Delta u-\mu |x|^{-2}u =\bigl(|\cdot|^{2-N}*|u|^p\bigr)|u|^{p-2}u \qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^N, \] where $|\cdot|^{2-N}$ is the Newton kernel, $p=\frac{N+2}{N-2}$, and $0<\mu<\frac{(N-2)^2}{4}$. For every $N\ge3$, we prove that positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb R^N)$ are radially symmetric about the origin, unique up to dilation, and nondegenerate. Our proof uses normalized logarithmic derivatives to obtain a cooperative system. The resulting monotonicity principle underlies both the uniqueness and nondegeneracy arguments, and remains effective in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$, corresponding to $N\ge7$. Consequently, the linearized quadratic form has Morse index one and the sharp inequality admits a global quadratic remainder estimate. The best constant is strictly concave in the Hardy parameter on $\bigl[0,\frac{(N-2)^2}{4}\bigr)$, is of class $C^2$ with strictly negative second derivative in the interior, and satisfies two-sided bounds that agree to first order at $\mu=0$.
item.dc:creator: Guangze Gu, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Non-Isothermal Plane Couette Flow for the Boltzmann Equation in Three Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Boltzmann equation for a non-isothermal plane Couette flow in the three-dimensional channel $\mathbb T_x\times(-1,1)_y\times\mathbb T_z$ for Maxwell molecules. For sufficiently small shear rate and wall temperature perturbations, we construct a unique steady solution near the global Maxwellian. For the corresponding unsteady boundary value problem, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions arising from small perturbations of the steady state, together with their exponential convergence to the steady state as $t\to\infty$. A major difficulty in both the steady and unsteady problems is to close the outgoing mass fluxes generated by diffuse reflection. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new boundary flux transmission framework which, in the slab geometry, yields steady and time-dependent wall flux estimates through the boundary-to-boundary transmission between the two walls. We further extend this framework to damped transport equations with diffuse reflection in general bounded $C^1$ domains, even when the damping coefficient degenerates at large velocities.
item.dc:creator: Zhida Chang, Mingying Zhong

item.title: Gradient potential estimates for k-Hessian equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $2\le k<n$, we prove pointwise gradient bounds for proper weak $k$-convex functions in terms of a local average and a Wolff potential of the full Hessian measure $F_k[u]$. The estimate yields local Lipschitz regularity for $F_k[u]=f$ with $f\in L^{n/k,1/k}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, and for $F_k[u]=|Du|^p$ when $0<p<nk/(n-k)$. Both the Lorentz index $1/k$ and the upper bound on $p$ are sharp.
item.dc:creator: Huajie Liu, Shiguang Ma, Shengyang Zang

item.title: Failure of P\'olya-Szeg\H{o} inequality for weighted nonlocal seminorm and on nonlocal C-K-N inequality
item.dc:creator: Prosenjit Roy, Vivek Sahu

item.title: Viscosity-variational inequality solutions of fully nonlinear second-order stationary mean field games with nonseparable and nondifferentiable Hamiltonians
item.description: arXiv:2611.08201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyse stationary fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic second-order mean field games with nonseparable and nondifferentiable Hamiltonians by introducing the notion of viscosity-variational inequality solution. In this formulation of the problem, the value function is the viscosity solution of the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, and the Kolmogorov--Fokker--Planck (KFP) equation for the player density is understood as a nonstandard variational inequality that no longer involves partial derivatives of the value function. The advantages of this formulation are found in its stability and continuity properties for handling weak convergence arguments, which we use to prove the existence of solutions of the problem. Furthermore, we prove the equivalence of the notion of viscosity-variational inequality solution with the notion of a partial differential inclusion solution, where the value function is a strong solution of the HJB equation and the player density is a very weak solution of the KFP equation with coefficients belonging to subdifferential sets of the Hamiltonian. Finally, we prove the uniqueness of solutions in the case of separable Hamiltonians with strictly monotone couplings.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sales, Iain Smears

item.title: Uniqueness of Extremizers and Convergence of the Euler-Lagrange Iteration for the Critical Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.08222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n \ge 3$, $2 \le \alpha < n$, and $1 < p,r < \infty$ satisfy $p^{-1}+r^{-1}=1+\alpha/n$. We prove uniqueness, up to common translations and dilations, of the normalized nonnegative extremizing pairs for the corresponding Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality. More generally, all positive finite-energy solutions of the Euler-Lagrange system belong to a single symmetry orbit. The proof compares two solutions at different relative scales. Total positivity of order two identifies the second eigenspace of an associated compact self-adjoint operator and forces each nonzero difference to change sign exactly once. The opposite orientations obtained at the two ends of the scale parameter then yield uniqueness. The same method proves radial nondegeneracy modulo dilation. We also establish strong convergence of the normalized alternating Euler-Lagrange iteration from every nonnegative, radially nonincreasing initial datum to a fixed extremizing pair, without rescaling the iterates. Square-root mass variables reduce the exclusion of several concentration profiles to a static spectral estimate and an energy-increment argument. The analysis includes sublinear exponents and the logarithmic borderline decay regimes.
item.dc:creator: Hanwen Lu

item.title: Shock solutions of a 3D spherical piston problem for the compressible Euler equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes the global well-posedness of shock solutions for a 3D spherical piston problem to the compressible Euler equations. The main mathematical challenges are the nonlinear coupling between the free shock boundary and the moving piston, alongside potential gradient catastrophes induced by spherical geometric source terms. To overcome these difficulties, we reformulate the problem using Riemann invariants and introduce a tailored directional derivative along the unperturbed piston trajectory. Then we can extend the local solution to construct a global piecewise smooth solution including a single shock under some moderate assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Pengfei Zhou, Huimin Yu, Xiaomin Zhang

item.title: Gradient higher integrability for a general class of degenerate parabolic double phase systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.08291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish quantitative local higher integrability estimates for weak solutions of degenerate parabolic systems with generalized double phase growth, whose prototype is $$u_t-\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{G'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du+a(x,t)\frac{H'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du\right)=0\qquad\text{in }\Omega_T.$$ Here $G$ and $H$ are Young functions satisfying suitable structural assumptions. The nonnegative coefficient $a$ is allowed to vanish and has a concave modulus of continuity $\omega$ with respect to the parabolic distance. For $\Psi(z,\varkappa)=G(\varkappa)+a(z)H(\varkappa)$, we prove that solutions in $L^\infty(0,T;L^s(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^N))$, $2\le s<\infty$, satisfy $\Psi(\cdot,|Du|)\in L^{1+\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, provided $$\limsup_{\rho \to 0+}\omega(\rho)\frac{H(\rho^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}{G(\rho^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}<\infty.$$ For bounded solutions, the corresponding condition involves $H(\rho^{-1})/G(\rho^{-1})$. These conditions extend the known interpolative gap bounds from power growth to general growth functions and continuity moduli. In particular, for $G(\varkappa)=\varkappa^p$, $H(\varkappa)=\varkappa^q$, and $\omega(\rho)\simeq\rho^\alpha$, they recover $q\le p+s\alpha/(n+s)$ and $q\le p+\alpha$, respectively. The proof combines an intrinsic stopping-time argument with inverse-function estimates to derive Poincar\'e and reverse H\"older inequalities adapted to the general growth phases.
item.dc:creator: Bogi Kim, Jehan Oh, Abhrojyoti Sen

item.title: On the elliptic regularization of maximal slope curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.08377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the so-called Weighted Energy-Dissipation approximation of gradient flows in metric spaces. We prove the convergence of minimizers to maximal slope curves under assumptions that are close to those of the original existence theory for metric gradient flows. The proof relies on an energy-dissipation identity for the approximating curves and on an adaptation of a general stability result for maximal slope curves.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Gobbino, Filippo Quattrocchi

item.title: Certified folding-free deformable image registration: A whole-cell Jacobian certificate and a sequential variational solver
item.description: arXiv:2611.06954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Registration maps propagate labels, measure local volume change, and map results back through their inverses; requiring invertibility. Voxelwise checks can miss folds between grid points. We study the canonical continuous extension of a nodal displacement field by trilinear interpolation and give a test that proves its Jacobian determinant positive in every grid cell or rejects the map. The test is rigorous under IEEE 754 binary64 arithmetic (correct rounding, no contraction). With a fixed boundary, certification implies a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of the image domain. We introduce SeqVP, built around this certificate. A proximal Jacobian-determinant-curl formulation yields inner problems whose penalties on changes in the map, Jacobian determinant, and curl vanish to first order at the current iterate. The method decreases a fixed outer energy up to a floating-point resolution guard and certifies every committed iterate. After certified initialization, stopping at any time returns a folding-free map. A Poisson-preconditioned gradient method with Jacobian-aware step prediction and affine-scaling damping, initialized by certified handoff from an uncertified binary32 pre-optimizer, handles a 1 mm brain MRI with about 2e7 unknowns in 90 s on one GPU. On 49 held-out OASIS pairs, SeqVP achieves mean Dice 0.821 over 35 structures and 0.889 over 4 tissue classes, with certified zero folding. Gains are 0.022 and 0.025 over ANTs SyN, and 0.022 and 0.023 over uniGradICON with instance optimization at equal time (paired, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), but maps are rougher. SeqVP is level with ANTs on LPBA40, behind it on IBSR18, and ahead of all label-free baselines on 20 large-deformation pairs. On fields from nine methods, the certificate finds non-positive-Jacobian cells in every ANTs SyN map (median 10, missed by voxelwise checks) and in maps from NiftyReg, ConvexAdam, uniGradICON, and TransMorph.
item.dc:creator: Baihan Zhao, Zicong Zhou, Guojun Liao

item.title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2611.07121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a divergence-free velocity field $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x},t)$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ that is a genuine function of position and carries both defining properties of turbulent transport: Richardson pair dispersion and a dissipative anomaly. No synthetic field has carried both, because the frame that gives the first destroys the field the second requires. The key is a dichotomy: deforming a spectrally localised pattern smears it across scales, whereas pushing its generating centres forward and re-convolving leaves the spectral envelope exactly invariant --- so transporting the eddy centres preserves both cascade and frame. In the field the finite-size Lyapunov exponent obeys $\zeta(R)=h(R)-1$ threshold by threshold within the scaling range, with a sweeping deficit $\Delta_{\rm sw}=+0.038\pm0.019$, consistent with zero, against $+0.091\pm0.019$ for the frozen field on the same data, a gap that doubles at Navier--Stokes intermittency. Companion papers prove that this family shows Richardson dispersion and a dissipative anomaly (Fefferman and Mayboroda 2026), and that a scalar advected by this flow obeys Yaglom's relation (De Lellis 2026), at small Kubo number. Trajectories forget their starting point as the smallest eddy is removed: the median separation of pairs released from one point with independent Brownian kicks varies as $\kappa_{p}^{0.0333\pm0.0038}$ over 22 decades of particle diffusivity, against $\kappa_{p}^{1/2}$ for a smooth control. A scalar in the same field closes the exact scale-by-scale variance budget, four independently measured terms balancing the dissipation to 15\% over 1.2 decades with no adjustable constant, and reaches its inertial--convective asymptote $S_{L}=-\chi r$ to $0.9995\pm0.0018$ once the measured diffusive transfer is restored, while under an imposed mean gradient $\chi$ changes by 14\% over a factor 5.8 in $\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Raul Jimenez, Svitlana Mayboroda, Camillo de Lellis, David N. Spergel, Max Engelstein

item.title: A Feynman-Kac Representation and Large Deviation Bounds for the Fisher-KPP Equation Driven by Finite-Activity Pure Jump Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.07868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic propagation speed of travelling wave solutions to the stochastic Fisher-KPP equation with multiplicative finite-activity pure jump L\'evy noise. The noise is represented by a compensated Poisson random measure with finite intensity, so that the solution evolves deterministically between successive jump times and undergoes multiplicative jumps at the event times. Our main contribution is a stochastic Feynman-Kac representation for the solution, which expresses the random field as the product of the exponential martingale of the jump noise and an expectation over the paths of an independent Brownian motion. This representation is the key probabilistic tool that converts the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation into an expectation problem, thereby allowing for a direct analysis of the front position. Building on this representation and on the large deviation analysis of the jump noise, we derive explicit upper and lower bounds for the asymptotic wave speed. These bounds are given in terms of the noise intensity $\epsilon$ and the L\'evy measure $\mu$, providing a quantitative description of how discontinuous stochastic forcing affects the propagation speed in the Fisher-KPP equation. Under the finite-activity assumption, a stopping-time iteration yields pathwise $L^\infty$ bounds and finite-speed propagation of the level sets of the front, which are essential for establishing the existence of a travelling wave profile. The framework extends naturally to multi-species cooperative systems, illustrating its robustness. Numerical simulations are included to demonstrate the informativeness of the theoretical speed bounds.
item.dc:creator: Yuhong Li, Hao Wen, Jianhua Huang

item.title: The stochastic Ginzburg-Landau equation with harmonic potential in the full subcritical regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.08038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we construct the complex Ginzburg-Landau dynamic associated with the harmonic oscillator, with a random force which is white in time and covers the full subcritical range in space. We are able to renormalise the non-linearity using the same constant as the one used to renormalise the problem associated to the Laplacian. By an extension of the problem to complex times, we are able to prove that the solution of the complex Ginzburg-Landau is equal in law to the solution of the purely dissipative case, i.e. the associated complex $\Phi^4$ model, but along a complex axis of time.
item.dc:creator: Sama\"el Mackowiak, Aur\'elien Minguella

item.title: The isoperimetric problem in the Riemannian Heisenberg $3$-space
item.description: arXiv:2611.08309v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every closed weakly stable constant mean curvature surface immersed in the Riemannian Heisenberg space ${\rm Nil}_3$ is an embedded rotational sphere. As a consequence, we solve the isoperimetric problem in ${\rm Nil}_3$: the isoperimetric domains of ${\rm Nil}_3$ are exactly the regions enclosed by rotational constant mean curvature spheres, and for each prescribed volume there is a unique such domain, up to ambient isometry. For small volumes, the isoperimetric result was proved by Tomter in 1993.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e M. Espinar, Pablo Mira

item.title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
item.description: arXiv:2611.08454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we prove that every complete noncompact two-sided properly embedded constant mean curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal. The result holds in every dimension. We assume no bounds on curvature or volume growth. This establishes the properly embedded case of the finite-index version of do Carmo's question. For nonzero mean curvature, we use the radii of inscribed balls to define a positive weight. This weight gives a polynomial bound on weighted volume, while its reciprocal satisfies a differential inequality involving the Jacobi operator. We combine these properties with stability outside a compact set to obtain finite total area. This leads to a contradiction.
item.dc:creator: Gongping Niu

item.title: Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
item.description: arXiv:1406.7675v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: (Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.) We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations. As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.
item.dc:creator: Khalil Chouk, Massimiliano Gubinelli, Guopeng Li, Jiawei Li, Tadahiro Oh

item.title: Comparison principles for degenerate sub-elliptic equations in non-divergence form
item.description: arXiv:2409.15144v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the comparison principle for viscosity sub- and super-solutions of degenerate quasi-linear equations in non-divergence form driven by the horizontal vector fields of a Carnot group, under an ellipticity condition and a homogeneity condition.
item.dc:creator: Juan J. Manfredi, Shirsho Mukherjee

item.title: Existence and multiplicity of $L^2$-Normalized solutions for the periodic Schr\"{o}dinger system of Hamiltonian type
item.description: arXiv:2504.15656v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the following nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger system of Hamiltonian type \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{array}{l} -\Delta u+V(x)u=\partial_v H(x,u,v)+\omega v,\ x \in \mathbb{R}^N, \\ -\Delta v+V(x)v=\partial_u H(x,u,v)+\omega u,\ x \in \mathbb{R}^N, \\ \displaystyle\int_{\R^N}|z|^2dx=a^2, \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} where the potential function $V(x)$ is periodic, $z:=(u,v):\R^N\rightarrow \R\times\R$, $\omega\in \R$ appears as a Lagrange multiplier, $a>0$ is a prescribed constant. The existence and multiplicity of $L^2$-normalized solutions for the above Schr\"{o}dinger system are obtained. The proof combines a constrained variational reduction, compactness estimates, and a Ljusternik--Schnirelmann type multiplicity theorem. In addition, a bifurcation result is also given.
item.dc:creator: Ruowen Qiu, Yuanyang Yu, Fukun Zhao

item.title: The Modified Camassa--Holm Equation with Step-Like Boundary Conditions: A Characterization of Existence
item.description: arXiv:2507.02100v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the modified Camassa-Holm equation \[ u_t+\left((u^2-u_x^2)m\right)_x=0,\quad m:= u-u_{xx}, \quad t>0,\ \ -\infty<x<+\infty \] subject to the step-like initial data: $u(x,0)\to A_1$ as $x\to-\infty$ and $u(x,0)\to A_2$ as $x\to+\infty$, where $0<A_1<A_2$. First, using the Riemann--Hilbert approach, we establish the global solvability of the corresponding problem in the reciprocal $(y,t)$-variables. Then the reconstruction in the original $(x,t)$-variables is obtained under a positivity condition expressed in terms of the solution of the associated Riemann--Hilbert problem.
item.dc:creator: I. Karpenko, D. Shepelsky, G. Teschl

item.title: Propagation of chaos for the Landau equation via microcanonical binary collisions
item.description: arXiv:2511.09035v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a fully constructive, conservative, and collision-level realization of Kac's program for the spatially homogeneous Landau equation across the full interaction range, including the Coulomb case. Our model is the microcanonical binary-collision (MBC) process: a reversible pure-jump $N$-particle Markov process, realizing the grazing-collision mechanism via small conservative rotations of relative velocities. Under suitable assumptions on the initial data, we prove propagation of chaos in the joint mean-field and grazing-collision limit ($N\to\infty, h\to0$), identifying any limit point with the unique solution in the relevant weak-solution class. The empirical measures converge in quadratic Wasserstein distance, while fixed-order marginals converge strongly in $L^1$ at every fixed time. Furthermore, we rigorously derive the Landau master equation as the fixed-$N$ grazing-collision limit of the MBC process. The proof combines Fisher-information dissipation, compactness, and uniqueness; for $\gamma\in[-3,-2)$, second-order information along collision directions yields the time-integrable $L^\infty$ bound needed for uniqueness.
item.dc:creator: Kai Du

item.title: Fully nonlinear second-order mean field games with nondifferentiable Hamiltonians
item.description: arXiv:2511.12780v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyse fully nonlinear second-order mean field games (MFG) with nondifferentiable Hamiltonians, which take the form of a coupled system of a fully nonlinear Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation and a Kolmogorov--Fokker--Planck partial differential inclusion (PDI) featuring the set-valued subdifferential of the Hamiltonian. We show the existence of solutions of some stationary MFG systems with quite general coupling operators and nonnegative distributional source terms, on general bounded convex domains, under the primary assumptions of uniform ellipticity and the Cordes condition on the diffusion coefficient. The existence proof is founded on an original, and equivalent, reformulation of the PDI as a nonstandard variational inequality (VI), that offers significant flexibility in passages to limits. Furthermore, the uniqueness of the solution of the PDI/VI system is proved in the case of strictly monotone couplings. We then show how the MFG PDI/VI system in the fully nonlinear setting can be obtained as the limit of a sequence of PDE systems with differentiable Hamiltonians, and we give further results on the continuous dependence of the solution.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sales, Iain Smears
