item.title: A Generalized Framework for Singular Fractional Burgers Equations with Stochastic Forcing
item.description: arXiv:2602.07492v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the regularization effect of fractional stochastic forcing on Burgers-type equations with fractional dissipation, with an application to the Degasperis--Procesi (DP) equation. In particular, we consider the perturbation induced by the singular noise $|D|^{1/2}\xi$ and establish local well-posedness in the negative Sobolev space $H^{-1/4+\delta}$ for some small $\delta>0$. Due to the singular nature of the nonlinear interactions, classical solution theories cannot be directly applied. Inspired by the framework developed in \cite{hairer2013solving,gubinelli2017kpz}, we introduce a generalized solution theory based on an enhanced structure and derive the effective equations satisfied by these generalized solutions. Our main contribution is the establishment of a general framework for describing singular PDEs driven by rough data. Moreover, we prove the convergence of the associated non-Gaussian rough structures in the fractional dissipation setting. As an application, we apply this framework to the stochastic Degasperis--Procesi equation and obtain its local well-posedness in the low-regularity regime.
item.dc:creator: Shuolin Zhang, Zhaonan Luo, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: A blow-up approach for a priori bounds in semilinear planar elliptic systems: the Brezis-Merle critical case
item.description: arXiv:2602.11720v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish uniform a priori estimates for solutions of semilinear planar Hamiltonian elliptic systems in a ball with Dirichlet boundary conditions. We consider a broad class of coupled nonlinearities with asymptotic critical behaviour in the sense of Brezis--Merle. The approach we follow is based on a blow-up analysis combined with Liouville--type theorems and integral estimates. Our results extend the scalar theory of uniform a priori bounds to the Hamiltonian case, and solve an open problem in [de Figueiredo D.G., do \'O J.M., Ruf B., Adv. Nonlinear Stud. 6 (2006), no. 2]. We believe that this approach is new in this setting. As a consequence of our a priori estimates, we prove the existence of a positive solution by means of fixed-point index theory.
item.dc:creator: Laura Baldelli, Gabriele Mancini, Giulio Romani

item.title: Inverse Semiclassical Scattering at Fixed Energy
item.description: arXiv:2609.02175v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate inverse scattering at a fixed energy for semiclassical Schr\"odinger operators with smooth potentials. For compactly supported potentials satisfying a natural virial condition, we prove that, under the sharp condition, $\liminf_{h\to0}\|S_1(\lambda,h)-S_2(\lambda,h)\|<2$ implies $V_1=V_2$, provided the fixed energy $\lambda$ lies above both potentials. We then consider radial short-range repulsive potentials. Under a monotonicity assumption on the radial force, we show that the semiclassical differential cross section at a fixed energy, up to $o(1)$ as $h\to0$, determines the potential in the classically accessible region. Finally, we obtain an analogous rigidity result for nontrapping compactly supported perturbations of the Euclidean metric under a strict convexity assumption.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Nicoleau

item.title: Non-simple blow-up for the Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on Riemannian surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.20042v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The existence and structure of non-simple blow-up are fundamental questions for the self-dual Chern--Simons--Higgs equation. Physically, this phenomenon describes magnetic-flux concentration in several cores whose mutual distances are much larger than their widths, although all cores approach the same vortex point. Despite substantial progress for singular Liouville equations, the existence of non-simple blow-up solutions to the full Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on closed surfaces has remained open in both the Chern--Simons (CS) and mean-field regimes. We prove that the cores of every non-simple cluster have equal limiting masses, share a common profile type, and form an asymptotically regular polygon. These identities yield an explicit finite list of admissible cluster masses and a four-unit mass-gap criterion. We also construct non-simple blow-up solutions on closed Riemannian surfaces in both regimes. Together, these results establish a sharp arithmetic criterion for single-point non-simple CS blow-up on each fixed flat torus when a suitable exterior divisor may be chosen, and show that vortex blow-up need not be simple, answering Li--Liu's question in the negative.
item.dc:creator: Youngae Lee, Lei Zhang

item.title: Symmetry and Monotonicity for Subcritical Fractional Hartree Equations with Singular Sets of Zero Capacity
item.description: arXiv:2610.24684v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study positive weak singular solutions of the subcritical fractional Hartree equation \[ (-\Delta)^s u = \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma} \frac{u^p(y)}{|x-y|^\mu}d y \right)u^q \quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma, \] where \(0<s<1\), \(N>2s\), \(0<\mu<N\), and \(\Gamma\subset\{x_1=0\}\) is compact with zero \((s,2)\)-capacity. For solutions with a nonremovable singular point on $\Gamma$, we prove hyperplane symmetry and strict transverse monotonicity under global Lebesgue integrability conditions. For $N\ge2$, we also prove these conclusions under upper bounds on $p$ and $q$, using only the integrability required for weak solutions. We also establish local regularity and construct solutions with logarithmic singularities along a line segment.
item.dc:creator: Guangze Gu, Aleks Jevnikar, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Radial conditions for global compact finite propagation for divergence-form elliptic operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.00876v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study global compact finite propagation (GCFP) for the wave equation $u_{tt}=\operatorname{div}(A(x)\nabla u)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, that is, the property that a disturbance starting in a compact set cannot reach spatial infinity in finite time. For smooth strictly positive matrices $A$ we show that GCFP implies $\int_1^\infty a_*(r)^{-1/2}\,dr=\infty$, where $a_*(r)$ is the minimum over the sphere of radius $r$ of $\langle A\omega,\omega\rangle$; the proof uses the equivalence of GCFP with completeness of the Riemannian metric $A^{-1}$, of which we prove the necessary direction for the cosine family of the Friedrichs extension. We also prove that the analogous divergence condition with $a^*(r)$, the maximum over the sphere, is sufficient, and that this holds for measurable coefficients $A\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with $A\ge I$. Finally, we construct a locally bounded measurable matrix with $a_*=a^*$ for which GCFP holds although the integral converges, so the necessary condition is not stable under the loss of continuity.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Perelmuter

item.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.03104v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.
item.dc:creator: Kaj Nystr\"om

item.title: Large time behavior of global solutions to one-dimensional non-isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations with large initial data
item.description: arXiv:2611.06309v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the construction of global solutions to the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional non-isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations, as well as the precise description of their large-time behavior. While results for small initial data are well-established, the case of large initial perturbations remains less satisfactory. Even for constant transport coefficients, only the Nishida-Smoller type solutions have been obtained so far. In this work, we will provide a complete resolution of this problem. The key idea involves revealing favorable hidden identities of the potential force and a new representation for the specific volume, which enables us to derive uniform upper and lower bounds on this quantity. Moreover, this strategy extends to compressible viscous single-ion flow under the Boltzmann relation; notably, this new method for deriving lower and upper bounds on the specific volume also applies to the Navier-Stokes equations. The proof relies on a domain decomposition technique and some new dissipative structures to close the nonlinear energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Lan Zhang, Huijiang Zhao

item.title: Borel Summability for Nonlinear Differential Systems on Characteristic Domains
item.description: arXiv:2201.04526v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate singularly perturbed nonlinear complex differential systems of the form $\hbar \partial_x f = F (x, \hbar, f)$, where $\hbar$ is a small complex perturbation parameter. We give geometric and analytic conditions under which the formal perturbative solution associated with a fixed regular leading-order branch is locally uniformly Borel summable. This leads to an existence and uniqueness theorem of holomorphic solutions with prescribed perturbative expansion. We give an explicit triangular example and a self-contained application to the singularly perturbed Painlev\'e I equation.

item.title: On a generalized Monge-Amp\`ere equation on closed almost K\"ahler surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2412.18361v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show the existence and uniqueness of solutions to a generalized Monge-Amp\`{e}re equation on closed almost K\"ahler surfaces, where the equation depends only on the underlying almost K\"ahler structure. As an application, we prove Donaldson's conjecture for tamed almost complex 4-manifolds.

item.title: On statistical inference for non-linear dynamical systems evolving in their global attractor
item.description: arXiv:2606.06018v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a periodic scalar reaction-diffusion system over a two-dimensional domain under natural conditions on the reaction function and with initial condition $\theta$. We show that on the global attractor $\mathcal A$ of the resulting dynamical system $(u_\theta(t):t>0)$, a reverse Poincar\'e inequality holds true, and that as a consequence the map $\theta \mapsto u_\theta(t)$ satisfies an $L^2(\Om)$-Lipschitz stability estimate on $\mathcal A$ for any $t>0$ fixed. We then show that statistical recovery of an initial condition $\theta$ in the attractor $\mathcal A$, as well as prediction of the states $u_\theta$, is possible from discrete measurements of the system at parametric $1/\sqrt N$ convergence rates.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Konen, Richard Nickl

item.title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.15984v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. Moreover, the perturbed foliation admits a common smooth calibration, hence the lifted leaves are area-minimizing. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.
item.dc:creator: Hoan Nguyen
